appearance.name: empty-patch
appearance.covers: A patch with nothing in it. Never touch /AP.

appearance.name: inert-keys-only
appearance.covers: Flags, reply relationship, group and the conversation plane. None of them is ever painted, so a change to all of them at once is still inert.

appearance.name: no-op-full-object-patch
appearance.covers: A client that sends the whole object back unchanged. Value-diffing is what stops that being a re-bake, and a classifier keyed on which keys are present would regenerate.

appearance.name: no-op-within-epsilon
appearance.covers: A rect that came back through an f32 round trip. A thousandth of a point is below anything visible and above the drift, so this is still inert.

appearance.name: clearing-an-explicitly-null-entry
appearance.covers: A tri-state clear of something the DTO already reports as null. Nothing changed.

appearance.name: clearing-an-entry-the-dto-omits
appearance.covers: A tri-state clear of a key the DTO does not carry AT ALL. Absent and null both mean the entry is not there, and a comparison that told them apart would re-bake for a write that changes nothing. The case above cannot catch that, because there both sides are null.

appearance.name: rect-translation
appearance.covers: The ordinary move: same size, new place, nothing else to carry.

appearance.name: resize-is-not-a-translation
appearance.covers: A rect that changed size. The pixels would be scaled rather than shifted, so /AP has to be re-baked.

appearance.name: markup-quads-ride-along
appearance.covers: A text markup whose quads move with the rect by the same delta.

appearance.name: markup-quads-left-behind
appearance.covers: The rect moved and the quads did not. The dictionary would desync from the pixels, so this is not a translation however much it looks like one.

appearance.name: markup-rect-only
appearance.covers: The rect moved and the quads were not mentioned. They are still on the annotation, unshifted, so the geometry is inconsistent and this regenerates.

appearance.name: vertices-ride-along
appearance.covers: A polygon whose vertices move with the rect.

appearance.name: ink-strokes-ride-along
appearance.covers: A nested array: the ink list is a list of point lists.

appearance.name: ink-advisory-rotation
appearance.covers: A vertex kind whose rotation scalar changed. Since 6153c181e the points are stored upright and the rotation turns them about the middle of their box when the appearance is drawn, so it regenerates even though nothing else changed.

appearance.name: box-rotation-changed
appearance.covers: A box kind whose rotation changed along with a move. The pixels rotate, so this is not a rigid translation.

appearance.name: box-rotation-preserved-by-omission
appearance.covers: A box kind with a rotation the patch does not mention. Omitted preserves, so the after-state matches and the move is rigid.

appearance.name: box-rotation-respelled
appearance.covers: A rotation written as 390 against a current 30. Those are the same angle and this still REGENERATES, because `rotation` is not in the subtype's translatable-geometry list: it lands in the touched set before the normalization inside the rigid-translation check can be reached. The normalization only ever runs for a rotation the patch omits or repeats verbatim.

appearance.name: box-rotation-repeated-verbatim
appearance.covers: The same move with the rotation repeated exactly. Value-diffing drops it before the touched set, so the move is rigid, which is the case that reaches the normalization at all.

appearance.name: unrotated-rect-left-behind
appearance.covers: The rect moved and the logical box did not. Preserved-yet-unshifted geometry fails the congruence check.

appearance.name: style-change
appearance.covers: A colour. Not geometry, so it re-bakes however little else moved.

appearance.name: contents-on-a-shape
appearance.covers: A shape's contents is popup note text and is never painted, so editing the comment must not destroy the appearance.

appearance.name: contents-on-free-text
appearance.covers: The same key on a kind whose /AP paints it. Here it re-bakes.

appearance.name: unknown-key
appearance.covers: A key from a newer client. Conservative by default.

appearance.name: unknown-subtype
appearance.covers: A subtype with no geometry table. Also conservative.

appearance.name: subtype-mismatch
appearance.covers: A patch for a different subtype than the annotation. Nothing about the geometry can be reasoned about across that.

appearance.name: link-move
appearance.covers: A link paints nothing of its own and is still in the geometry table, so a move classifies as a translation rather than asking for an /AP that does not exist.

appearance.name: callout-line-rides-along
appearance.covers: A free text's leader line moves with its box.

appearance.name: geometry-appearing
appearance.covers: A move that also adds geometry the annotation did not have. Something appeared, so nothing was merely translated.

appearance.name: line-points-ride-along
appearance.covers: A line annotation whose two endpoints move with the rect.
